tips.text: Land Steel Tempest on enemy champions or minions to build two stacks, then your next one fires a whirlwind that knocks up from range.
Dash through a minion with Sweeping Blade to close in or escape, but keep one nearby so you still have a way out.
Cast Steel Tempest while dashing with Sweeping Blade to hit everyone around you, which is an easy way to build your stacks.
Put up Wind Wall when the enemy fires a projectile at you, like an arrow or a spell. It blocks enemy projectiles but not melee attacks.
Keep moving in lane to charge your shield from Way of the Wanderer. Trade when it is full, since it absorbs the first hit you take.
Save Last Breath for when an enemy is knocked up, even by an ally. It teleports you to them and holds nearby knocked up enemies in the air.
Sweeping Blade can't hit the same target again for a while, so pick dash targets with that in mind. Hitting different targets in a row makes it hit harder.

combos.name: Last Breath through Q
combos.when: When an ally or your own whirlwind has knocked an enemy up and you want a quick, safe engage.
combos.text: Hold Q during the dash and cast R while the dash is still going. The ultimate lands, and the circle Q hits around where you blink to.

tips.text: Land Steel Tempest on enemy champions or minions to build two stacks, then your next one fires a whirlwind that knocks enemies up.
Use Wind Wall when a dangerous projectile is coming, such as a mage's main spell or an arrow volley. It blocks enemy projectiles.
Dash through minions with Sweeping Blade to close in or escape. Keep one nearby for an exit before you dash at the enemy.
Cast Steel Tempest while dashing with Sweeping Blade to hit everything around you. With two stacks, that circle knocks enemies up.
Save Last Breath for when an enemy is airborne, from your whirlwind or an ally's spell. You can't cast it on anyone on the ground.
Keep moving in lane so Way of the Wanderer fills up. Its shield then absorbs the first hit you take from a champion.
Sweeping Blade can't hit the same target again for a while. Dash through other minions to keep moving, and don't plan on re-dashing the same target.

combos.name: Dash-buffered Q knock-up
combos.when: When Yasuo has two stacks and an enemy is close to a minion or to Yasuo's dash path.
combos.text: Press Q while dashing so it fires at the end of the dash as a circle. With two stacks the knock-up lands instantly, with no wind-up that the enemy can see.

combos.name: Knock-up into Last Breath
combos.when: When you want to follow a knock-up with the ultimate, either your own or one from an ally.
combos.text: Buffer R during the Q cast so it fires the instant the cast ends. This leaves the enemy almost no time to react.

combos.name: Flash buffered Q at the end of a dash
combos.when: When an enemy is just out of dash range and you hold two stacks.
combos.text: Dash, buffer Q, then Flash toward the target. The circle hits at the Flash landing spot, so the knock-up reaches farther than the dash alone.

tips.text: Dash through minions with Sweeping Blade to close distance or escape. The same target can't be dashed again for a while, so keep other minions nearby.
Land Steel Tempest on enemies or minions twice to charge a whirlwind. It knocks enemies up and travels past the first thing it hits.
Put Wind Wall in front of you or your support when enemy arrows or spells are coming. It blocks enemy projectiles, so use it in the middle of a trade.
Last Breath works on any enemy knocked up, even by your support. Ask your support to start fights with a knock up, then follow with Last Breath.
Keep moving to fill your Way of the Wanderer shield. It triggers when a champion hits you, so walk around before you trade.

combos.name: Steel Tempest through dash (E-Q)
combos.when: When dashing onto a minion or enemy and you want a circular Q on the people around you, especially with a stored tornado.
combos.text: Press Q while the dash is still going. It hits in a circle around you when the dash ends, and with two stacks it knocks everyone nearby up.

tips.text: Put Wind Wall in front of Infernal Chains; it destroys the chain, so you aren't slowed or pulled back.
The Darkin Blade is slow and shows where it will land. Step sideways out of the hit zone, or dash out with Sweeping Blade.
Aatrox's Umbral Dash can't be blocked, so don't count on Wind Wall to stop it. Wind Wall only stops projectiles like Infernal Chains.
Hold Steel Tempest stacks for when The Darkin Blade is on cooldown. Then the whirlwind knocks him up and you can trade freely.
Aatrox heals when he hits you, so don't trade into his empowered Deathbringer Stance attack. Wait until it's used, then fight.
Put Wind Wall in front of Briar's Chilling Scream when she charges it. It is a projectile, so the wall blocks it.
Briar's Head Rush stuns you, so keep Sweeping Blade ready to dash away once she lands on you.
Keep minions or targets near you as dash targets. Sweeping Blade lets you leave when Briar goes into Blood Frenzy.
Fight Briar when she is low on health. Her Crimson Curse heals her as she hits you, so long trades favor her.
Stay away from walls when Briar charges Chilling Scream. A full charge knocks you back, and hitting a wall stuns you.
Keep Steel Tempest narrow thrusts on Darius, but stay away from his range; his Decimate hurts most when you are inside it.
Put Wind Wall up when Darius is about to pull you; it won't block Apprehend, so instead walk out of the cone's direction.
Poke Darius while Apprehend is on cooldown, then back off when it returns.
Don't trade with Darius while you carry many Hemorrhage stacks; Noxian Guillotine can finish you.
Don't knock Fiora up when Riposte is ready; she can parry it and stun you.
Bait Riposte with a weak Steel Tempest, then go in once she has used it.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when she has to use a projectile; it blocks Riposte's stab.
Watch the Vital on you; she will try to Lunge from that direction, so step away when it lines up.
Use Sweeping Blade through minions to dodge her Lunge and keep space.
Wind Wall blocks Parrrley and keg shots. Cast it when Gangplank lines up a shot at you.
Dash away with Sweeping Blade when kegs are near you; a keg explosion slows you and hurts a lot.
Attack a keg yourself to defuse it, so it can't be used against you.
Gangplank cleanses crowd control with Remove Scurvy, so wait for it before committing your knock up combo.
Dodge sideways when Garen swings Decisive Strike at you; his silence stops your dash and your Wind Wall.
Do not stand in Garen's Judgment; leave its range or put minions around you so it deals less to you.
Run from Garen once your health is low, because Demacian Justice finishes you quickly.
Poke Garen with Steel Tempest from range and keep him from getting a few quiet seconds, so Perseverance does not heal him.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Jayce lines up Shock Blast; it destroys the bolt.
Jayce is strong early. Play safe if he gets ahead, and farm until you can trade.
Watch for his Acceleration Gate; a gate on the ground usually means a stronger Shock Blast is coming.
Jayce's Thundering Blow knocks you back, so don't dash in close when it is ready.
Land two Steel Tempest hits to fire a tornado. If it knocks Jayce up, you can follow with Last Breath.
Keep Wind Wall ready for the empowered Ntofo Strikes shockwave; it is a projectile and the wall destroys it before you are pulled in and stunned.
Do not walk into K'Sante while he charges Path Maker; he takes less damage and the charge cannot be interrupted. Step aside and let the dash miss.
Last Breath needs an airborne enemy. The pull and knock back from K'Sante are not knock ups, so look for your own Steel Tempest whirlwind to set it up.
When K'Sante goes All Out, he is much squishier and has less health, so trade hard with Steel Tempest and Sweeping Blade. Do not let him catch you.
Stay away from walls when K'Sante is close. All Out sends you through terrain and he strikes you again.
Do not dash with Sweeping Blade toward K'Sante when his Footwork shield is up; wait for it to fade, then trade.
Dodge Seismic Shard's slow by keeping your distance when Malphite has it ready; being slowed lets him catch you.
Use Wind Wall to block Seismic Shard before it lands. It is a projectile, so the wall stops it.
Avoid fighting Malphite while his Granite Shield is up; wait until it breaks.
Ground Slam cuts your Attack Speed, so step out of its range before you fight.
Stand behind minions when Mordekaiser is near, and dash away sideways when his Death's Grasp is cast; it lands after a short delay.
Put Wind Wall in front of Death's Grasp; it blocks the claw's projectile.
Do not stand in melee for long once Mordekaiser has Darkness Rise; poke with Steel Tempest and step out before the aura wears you down.
Hold your damage when his Indestructible shield is up; hit him after it fades.
Keep your distance from Mordekaiser at level 6; Realm of Death cuts you off from allies and from Wind Wall.
Put Wind Wall up when Rumble casts Electro Harpoon at you; it blocks the harpoon and stops his slow.
Rumble cannot cast spells while Overheated, so go in on him then.
Do not stand in The Equalizer's fire; walk out with Sweeping Blade through a minion rather than staying slowed in it.
Do not stay in front of Flamespitter; dash out of its cone instead of standing in it.
Hold your shield from Way of the Wanderer for when Rumble starts his trade; it absorbs damage from his champion hits.
Sidestep Decimating Smash when you see Sion charging. The stun is long once he has held it, so keep your distance.
Put up Wind Wall to block Roar of the Slayer when Sion fires it. It does not stop Decimating Smash.
Dash away with Sweeping Blade when Sion starts charging Decimating Smash. Keep a minion close so you can leave.
Attack Sion when his Soul Furnace shield is gone, since the shield absorbs your damage. Step out before it blows up.
Do not chase Sion into a kill. Glory in Death brings him back with fast hits, so walk away from him when he revives.
Stay out of a straight line with Sion at level 6, since Unstoppable Onslaught cannot be turned much.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Teemo throws Blinding Dart; it blocks the dart and the blind.
Don't walk through bushes or onto likely spots without care. Noxious Trap is stealthed, and it slows and reveals you.
Don't hit and back out, since Toxic Shot's poison keeps hurting you. Stay at a safe range until you are ready to commit.
Use Sweeping Blade through minions to close the gap on Teemo quickly, then hit him with Steel Tempest.
Don't walk up to Vayne near walls; Condemn knocks you back and stuns you if you hit terrain.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Vayne fires Condemn; it blocks projectiles.
Vayne is fragile, so dash in with Sweeping Blade on a minion and pressure her. She has to play carefully.
Break up her third attack: Silver Bolts resets when she switches targets, so back off for a moment when she has two hits on you.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Yone's Mortal Steel whirlwind comes; it is a missile and the wall destroys it.
Don't wall Spirit Cleave; it is not blocked by projectile walls. Step out of its cone instead, since it cannot hit anyone behind Yone.
Land two Steel Tempest hits to knock Yone up, then use Last Breath for a big burst.
Dodge Yone's Mortal Steel sideways; the thrust is narrow. Trade back while his cooldown is down.
Back off when Yone enters spirit form with Soul Unbound; he stores damage and hits again when it ends.
Dodge Charm sideways or keep a minion between you and Ahri; it stops at the first enemy it hits.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Ahri aims Charm or Orb of Deception; it destroys her projectiles.
Once Ahri has used Charm, step in with Sweeping Blade and trade, since she has no easy way to stop you.
Fight Ahri while Spirit Rush is on cooldown; she has a hard time getting away.
If Ahri charms you or an ally and you are knocked up, Last Breath can follow up on an airborne enemy champion.
Use Wind Wall to block Akali's Five Point Strike and Shuriken Flip when she commits to a trade.
Fight Akali when her energy is low. Her Five Point Strike is much weaker then.
Her Twilight Shroud hides her, but area damage still hits her and briefly shows where she is. Use Steel Tempest into the smoke.
Play safe when Akali has Perfect Execution ready, especially if you are low on health.
Dash away with Sweeping Blade after her Perfect Execution lands. Her second dash needs time to come back.
Put Wind Wall up when Akshan throws Avengerang; it blocks the boomerang, so he loses his poke and his speed boost.
Use Wind Wall against Comeuppance bullets and the shots from Heroic Swing; they are projectiles and the wall stops them.
Akshan has no hard crowd control, so pick the fights you want and dash in with Sweeping Blade.
Step sideways out of Avengerang. It is narrow, but it comes back, so watch the return path too.
Look for Akshan after he uses Heroic Swing; a stun or knock up while he swings can cancel it, and Steel Tempest's whirlwind knocks up.
Use Wind Wall on Flash Frost and Frostbite; blocking them removes most of her damage. Cast it when she looks ready to throw.
Never dash with Sweeping Blade toward Crystallize; the wall can shove you aside and cost your trade. Use another target or wait for the wall to melt.
Dodge Flash Frost sideways; if it stuns you, you are open to Frostbite. Do not walk straight at her.
Attack her egg once Rebirth triggers and she cannot act; with help, kill it. Do not dive into her when she is healthy.
Step out of Glacial Storm quickly; it grows over time and slows you the longer you stay inside.
Watch Annie's Pyromania counter. When it is full, stay out of her range or keep a minion handy to dash away, because her stun will leave you helpless.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Annie casts Disintegrate. It blocks her fireball.
Engage right after she spends her stun or her spells. Sweeping Blade lets you close the gap quickly.
Stay away from Tibbers once he appears. He burns everything near him.
Put Wind Wall in front of Aurelion Sol's Breath of Light and Falling Star when he starts casting.
Don't dash into the middle of Singularity; it drags you in and can finish you off at low health.
Dash through minions with Sweeping Blade to close on Aurelion Sol, then thrust Steel Tempest to build toward your whirlwind.
When The Skies Descend knocks you up, Last Breath is not available to you from it; avoid the big impact, and save Last Breath for enemies you knock up.
Put Wind Wall in front of Twofold Hex; it blocks the bolt. Aurora's Twofold Hex recast also fires back as a projectile, so it can be blocked too.
Aurora's The Weirding blast is not blocked by Wind Wall, so sidestep it instead.
Dash in with Sweeping Blade on a minion to close the gap, then trade when The Weirding is on cooldown.
Aurora turns invisible after Across the Veil. Don't chase blindly; walk back and farm until she shows up again.
Her Between Worlds rift slows you when you cross its edge. Stay out of it, or wait for it to close before you go in.
Cast Wind Wall when Azir's Sand Soldiers dash at you with Conquering Sands; the notes say soldiers stop when they hit it.
Fight when Azir's Sand Soldiers are stationary or gone. He deals most of his damage through them, so trade right after they expire.
Dash onto Azir with Sweeping Blade to close the gap fast. He lacks upfront burst, so a quick all-in can beat him.
Stay away from Emperor's Divide when you are close to Azir; it knocks you back and leaves a wall you cannot walk through.
Land two Steel Tempest hits on a minion or champion, then use the whirlwind to knock Azir up.
Dodge Sear sideways; it is narrow and stops at the first unit it hits. Standing behind a minion also blocks it.
Put Wind Wall between you and Brand when he starts Pyroclasm or Sear. It destroys the projectile, so save it for his key spells.
Wind Wall will not stop Conflagration, so stay out of its range or move away from allies and minions.
Walk out of Pillar of Flame as soon as it appears. It lands after a short delay, so step away.
Close in with Sweeping Blade through minions once Brand's Sear is on cooldown. He has little defense up close.
Step away from your team when Pyroclasm is cast. It bounces between enemies, and its first missile is slow enough to react.
Put Wind Wall in front of Briar's Chilling Scream; it is a projectile, so the wall stops it.
Briar's Certain Death starts with a kicked projectile. Wind Wall blocks it, so hold it for her level 6 and she can't reach you.
Stay away from walls when Briar charges Chilling Scream fully; hitting a wall makes it hurt a lot and stuns you.
Dash away with Sweeping Blade using a minion when Briar leaps in with Head Rush; she is vulnerable once her stun ends.
Hit Steel Tempest twice and send the whirlwind when Briar commits; it knocks her up, which sets up Last Breath.
Cast Wind Wall at Cassiopeia's Noxious Blast and Twin Fang; it blocks projectiles and costs her a lot of damage.
Don't dash into Miasma; you get grounded and slowed, so Sweeping Blade can't get you out.
Turn away from Cassiopeia as she casts Petrifying Gaze so you get slowed, not stunned.
Weave Sweeping Blade through minions to close the gap, then hit her with Steel Tempest.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Diana aims Crescent Strike; it destroys the bolt.
Step sideways out of Crescent Strike; if you are marked with Moonlight, Diana can dash to you with Lunar Rush, so back off.
Wait out the Pale Cascade orbs and shield before you fight; the orbs only last a few seconds.
Hold Sweeping Blade on a minion near Diana, not on her, so you have a dash ready to leave after Moonfall.
Keep your distance from Diana at level 6, since Moonfall pulls you in and slows you.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Ekko throws Timewinder; it destroys the projectile and keeps you from being slowed.
Wind Wall does not stop the Parallel Convergence sphere. Walk out of the area instead, or dash away with Sweeping Blade.
Watch for the Parallel Convergence image on the ground. Leave the area before Ekko steps in, or you get stunned.
Trade right after Ekko spends Timewinder, and save Sweeping Blade for dodging his next dash-in.
Steel Tempest's whirlwind knocks Ekko up, so use Last Breath on him if you can. Do not chase once he has Chronobreak ready.
Put Wind Wall between you and Ezreal when he lines up Mystic Shot or Essence Flux; it destroys his projectiles.
Dash through minions with Sweeping Blade to close in on Ezreal, since he is fragile and you should take the fight to him.
Hold Wind Wall for Trueshot Barrage; it blocks the arc, which is his big damage.
Expect Ezreal to blink away with Arcane Shift when you commit, so dash again or fire your whirlwind to catch him.
Aim Wind Wall at Fizz's Chum the Waters lure; it stops the lure early.
Do not chase Fizz into Playful. He is untargetable, then slows you, so wait for it to land.
Urchin Strike does no damage if you are untargetable or dash away, so use Sweeping Blade on a minion to dodge it.
Fizz's Seastone Trident glows before his empowered hit. Back away from the trade until it is used.
Keep a minion near for Sweeping Blade so you can escape after Fizz's Chum the Waters lands.
Put Wind Wall in front of Winds of War; it blocks both windblasts.
Do not walk into Galio while he charges Shield of Durand; it can taunt you into Justice Punch.
Galio is slow while charging Shield of Durand, so poke him with Steel Tempest from range.
Last Breath works on Galio's knock up, even his own Justice Punch, so use it on a Galio ally or on Galio's target.
Watch for Hero's Entrance; it can be interrupted before Galio jumps, so hit him then.
Cast Wind Wall at Hwei's fireball or Gaze of the Abyss eye missile; it destroys them. It won't stop his lightning bolt or jaws.
Rush Hwei right after he casts a Torment spell; his spells take time to cast, and he is easy to close in on afterward.
Keep moving and sidestep his fireball, since Hwei must predict your path.
Keep moving so the Severing Bolt lightning lands behind you. It hits harder when you are alone or can't move, so stay near minions.
Use Sweeping Blade through minions to close the gap fast, and skip the dash when Hwei is close to rooting or dragging you.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Irelia casts Flawless Duet or Vanguard's Edge; it destroys the blades and the stun never lands.
Fight Irelia when her Ionian Fervor stacks have dropped; she is much weaker without the attack speed.
Watch for the bladed lines of Flawless Duet; stepping out of the line avoids the stun.
Don't spend your big abilities into Defiant Dance; she takes much less damage while charging. Wait for her to release.
Avoid fighting beside a full minion wave; Irelia uses Bladesurge on minions to reach you. Dash through minions yourself to keep your own escape.
Kassadin's Void Stone cuts magic damage, and Sweeping Blade deals magic damage. Poke him with Steel Tempest instead.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Kassadin casts Null Sphere; it blocks the orb and his shield.
Don't stand in Force Pulse range for long; it slows you and ruins your dashes.
Wind Wall cannot stop Force Pulse, so dodge it by staying out of its short range.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Katarina throws Bouncing Blade. It blocks the dagger.
Keep Wind Wall ready for Death Lotus. It blocks her projectiles, and her daggers are projectiles.
Fight Katarina right after she uses Shunpo; her short mobility cooldown is gone and she can't escape easily.
Stay away from the Daggers on the ground; she uses them for damage and to reset Shunpo.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when LeBlanc throws Ethereal Chains or Sigil of Malice. It destroys her projectiles and protects you.
Move sideways to dodge Ethereal Chains. If it lands, break away before the tether ends so you don't get rooted.
Attack LeBlanc right after she dashes with Distortion. Her return is her escape, so a stun or silence can stop it.
Don't chase the clone made by Mirror Image. The real LeBlanc is invisible only briefly, so look for her.
Use Sweeping Blade on minions to close the gap on LeBlanc and dodge her follow-up. Keep a minion nearby as your escape.
Don't dash into Lissandra with Sweeping Blade while Ring of Frost is ready; you will be rooted and punished.
Put Wind Wall in front of you to block Ice Shard and Glacial Path when she throws them.
Engage when Ring of Frost is on cooldown; it has a long cooldown early.
Approach from behind your minions so Ice Shard hits them first and you avoid being slowed.
Use Steel Tempest's whirlwind to knock her up when she is in range, then follow with Last Breath.
Stun her out of Glacial Path before she recasts it, or she will blink away.
Walk to the side and use Wind Wall against Light Binding. Keep it ready for when Lux is about to throw it.
Wind Wall does not stop Final Spark. Move out of the line when you see the red targeting beam.
Dash in with Sweeping Blade through minions to close the gap, then trade quickly. Lux is weak up close.
Do not stand in Lucent Singularity. Dash out or around it so you are not slowed.
Hit Lux with Steel Tempest twice, then fire the whirlwind to knock her up if she is rooted or close.
Hold Wind Wall back; it is your only way to stop Call of the Void.
Sidestep Call of the Void. Walk out of the area between the portals before it fires.
Stay away from minions carrying Malefic Visions. When they die, the visions spread to you.
Hit Malzahar when his Void Shift is down; while it is active he takes very little damage and ignores crowd control.
Dash to Malzahar with Sweeping Blade when his Nether Grasp is down, since he is helpless to its suppression.
Do not rely on Wind Wall to stop Mel's Rebuttal or Solar Snare cleanly; keep it for her Radiant Barrage, which is made of missiles the wall can block.
Put Wind Wall between you and Solar Snare when she aims at you; the orb is a projectile and the wall blocks it.
Sidestep Solar Snare, since it is a narrow line, and do not dash into the field it leaves behind, which slows you.
Trade right after Mel spends Rebuttal, when her shield and projectile block are down.
Step away for a moment when Mel has hit you many times; her stored Overwhelm damage can execute you when you are low.
Dash through minions with Sweeping Blade to close on Mel, and finish with Steel Tempest when she is in reach.
Wait for Mel to be knocked up by Steel Tempest's whirlwind, then use Last Breath for a big hit on her.
Put Wind Wall in the way of Darkin Daggers; it blocks all enemy projectiles, so her poke and heal setup never lands.
Dodge Darkin Daggers sideways and don't stand in a line with her; it is a thrown blade that bleeds you if it hits.
Hit her with Steel Tempest twice to knock her up, then use Last Breath when she is in the air.
Don't chase her while she is untargetable after The Call of the Pack or in Hounds' Pursuit. Wait for it to end, then trade.
Use Sweeping Blade on minions to dodge Eviscerate or to close the gap after she lands.
Cast Wind Wall to block Command: Attack when the Ball is thrown at you; it also stops her Command: Protect on allies.
Orianna only affects the area around the Ball, so check where it sits before you dash in with Sweeping Blade.
Do not dash into her Ball's area at level 6; Command: Shockwave pulls you in and stuns you.
Dodge Command: Attack sideways; it is thin, and she must wait for the Ball to return before using it again.
Her Ball knocking you into a bad spot can set up a Last Breath for your allies' knock ups, so save it for them.
Put Wind Wall up against Elemental Wrath when she throws it at you; the Rock, River and Brush blades are all projectiles and get blocked.
Wind Wall can't stop Audacity, because it is a dash and not a projectile. Keep Sweeping Blade ready to dash away when she jumps on you.
Do not walk into her stun wall. Supreme Display of Talent is blocked by Wind Wall, but the shockwave along the terrain is not.
Qiyana gets stronger when she is next to walls, river or brush. Fight her in the open lane, away from terrain she can use.
Stay out of river and brush edges near her; Supreme Display of Talent can leave you stunned there.
After she uses Terrashape, her Elemental Wrath comes back quickly. Trade after she has spent her abilities, not before.
Dash onto a minion with Sweeping Blade to close on Ryze, then slash with Steel Tempest.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Ryze casts Spell Flux or Overload. It destroys projectiles.
Do not walk into Ryze while he has Flux on you. His Rune Prison would root you.
Attack Ryze while his portal is charging. Crowd control on him cancels Realm Warp.
Stand behind minions when Sylas is ready to throw Chain Lash; Wind Wall is your answer to Abduct, so keep it up before he tries to pull you.
Cast Wind Wall when Sylas throws his chains with Abscond / Abduct; the chains are blocked, so he cannot pull himself to you.
Trade when Sylas has just spent his abilities; his Petricite Burst hits hard right after he casts, so avoid fighting him while he holds charges.
Do not fight when Sylas is low and Kingslayer is ready; it heals him back up. Burst him down instead of trading slowly.
Sylas's Abduct knocks you up, which lets Last Breath work on enemies he pulled. Save your ultimate for fights where he or an ally knocks someone up.
Dash through minions with Sweeping Blade to close in, but keep one nearby. Syndra's Scatter the Weak can punish you if you have no dash left.
Put up Wind Wall when Syndra is about to throw Force of Will or push spheres with Scatter the Weak. It blocks them.
Walk around spheres on the ground, and attack just after Syndra uses Scatter the Weak. Its long cooldown leaves her open.
Steel Tempest is narrow, so use it to hit Syndra when she is close. Two hits give you a whirlwind that knocks her up from range.
Do not stand in the zone of the spheres when she has her ultimate. Unleashed Power hits harder with more spheres out and executes low health targets.
Put Wind Wall in front of Threaded Volley; it blocks the rocks and the boulder, so you can walk up and trade.
Do not dash over her stones with Sweeping Blade; they detonate and leave you stunned.
Step sideways when she throws Threaded Volley, because the rocks fly in a fixed direction.
Once you land two Steel Tempests, her Seismic Shove knocks you out of position, so stay away from her stones after she casts it.
Fight right after she wastes Unraveled Earth or Seismic Shove; her lane control is weakest while they are on cooldown.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Talon throws Rake; it destroys the blades and denies his Wound stacks.
Avoid taking a Rake plus Noxian Diplomacy combo. Three Wound stacks and an attack make Blade's End bleed you hard.
Talon can vault walls and vanish with Shadow Assault. Watch the map and don't overextend when he disappears.
Chain Steel Tempest on minions to build the whirlwind, then use it to hit Talon and knock him up when he dives.
Dash with Sweeping Blade through a minion to dodge Talon's burst, and save your shield by moving until you need it.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Twisted Fate throws Wild Cards; it blocks the cards.
Dodge to the side of Wild Cards; the cards fan out, so move out of the cone.
Back off when the Gold Card is locked in; a stun lets him hit you for free. Wait out his shuffle and then step in.
When Destiny goes off, expect him to jump on you or a lane. Move toward safety and keep Wind Wall ready.
Cast Wind Wall when Veigar aims Baleful Strike at you; it blocks the bolt.
Dark Matter lands after a delay with a visible marker, so walk out of the circle instead of fighting in it.
Don't dash through the edge of Event Horizon; stay inside it or wait for it to fade, since only the edge stuns.
Veigar is fragile, so go in with Sweeping Blade through minions once Event Horizon is used.
Stay healthy before level 6; Primordial Burst hurts more the lower you are.
Put Wind Wall in front of Mistral Bolt and Looming Darkness. Both are projectiles, so the wall stops them before they reach you.
Vex fears and interrupts dashes when her passive is ready, so hold Sweeping Blade until she has spent her empowered ability.
Each dash you make marks you when you are near Vex, so her next hit deals bonus damage. Dash only when it wins you something.
Dodge Mistral Bolt sideways, since the wave is narrow when it speeds up. Then walk in and trade while it recharges.
Wind Wall can't stop Personal Space, which hits everyone around Vex. Stay out of its range or accept the trade.
Keep your distance from Vex and block her Shadow Surge with Wind Wall. She can't be knocked up easily, so use Steel Tempest on her lane partners instead.
Use Wind Wall against Hextech Ray when Viktor fires it, so you can walk up to him.
Don't dash into Gravity Field. Go around it or wait for it to expire, because staying inside gets you stunned.
Dodge Siphon Power's shield by trading right after it is used. Use Steel Tempest and Sweeping Blade on minions to get close to Viktor.
Step out of Arcane Storm's area when you can; it follows you, so move away from it as it comes.
Dodge Transfusion's damage by dashing out of range with Sweeping Blade. Don't stay in range for long trades, since he heals through them.
Don't use Steel Tempest into Sanguine Pool. Vladimir can't be targeted, so wait until the pool ends.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Vladimir charges Tides of Blood. It destroys the bolts.
Step out of Vladimir's Hemoplague circle. Hit him before it bursts, or he heals.
Close the distance on Xerath with Sweeping Blade through minions. He is weak up close and has few ways to escape.
Put up Wind Wall when Xerath aims Shocking Orb at you. It blocks the orb and saves you from the stun.
Step sideways to dodge Arcanopulse; it is narrow and hard to hit when you move side to side.
Dodge Eye of Destruction by walking out of the marked circle before it lands.
Move away from Xerath's Rite of the Arcane circles when you see him start channeling; each shot lands after a short delay.
Hold Steel Tempest stacks for a whirlwind to poke Xerath from range, but don't fire it into a Shocking Orb you can't dodge.
Dodge Xin Zhao's Wind Becomes Lightning sideways, or put Wind Wall in front of it; the thrust slows you.
Back away when Xin Zhao has his third Three Talon Strike ready; it knocks you up.
Wait until Xin Zhao has spent Audacious Charge before you trade, because it is how he closes on you.
Keep Sweeping Blade targets nearby so you can dash away from Xin Zhao's all-in.
Stay clear of Xin Zhao at level 6; Crescent Guard knocks you back and stuns you if you are not Challenged.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Yone throws the whirlwind from Mortal Steel; the wall stops it, so you aren't knocked up.
Don't spend Wind Wall on Spirit Cleave. It isn't blocked by projectile walls, so dodge it or move out of the cone instead.
Watch Yone's stacks. When he has two, his next Mortal Steel dashes and knocks you up, so step back out of range or sidestep it.
Wait for Yone to use Spirit Cleave, then trade. He can't shield again for a while.
Back off while Yone is in spirit form from Soul Unbound. Hits on you are stored and come back as extra damage when it ends.
Respect Yone at level 6. Fate Sealed hits a long way, so keep Wind Wall in mind and don't stand in a line with him.
Use Last Breath when Yone's own knock up or an ally's lands on an enemy. Any airborne enemy champion works.
Put Wind Wall in front of Zed's Razor Shuriken; it blocks projectiles, so his main poke and his shadow's throw do nothing.
Zed becomes untargetable when he starts Death Mark, so wait for the mark to land before you fight. Then stay on your feet and avoid trading until it pops.
Trade right after Zed uses Living Shadow. His damage and mobility depend on it, so he is weakest then.
Hit Steel Tempest on Zed twice to get the whirlwind. Use it when you want to knock him up, then follow with Last Breath.
Dash away with Sweeping Blade when Zed's shadow and Zed are about to slash together, because overlapping slashes slow you more.
Dodge sideways when Zoe throws Sleepy Trouble Bubble. Wind Wall can also block it, so save it for that.
Put up Wind Wall against Paddle Star! so it never reaches you.
Close the distance on Zoe quickly with Sweeping Blade through minions. Her star hurts most at long range.
Punish Zoe when she uses Portal Jump. She has to come back to her start point, so go at her then.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Ashe fires Volley or Enchanted Crystal Arrow. It blocks them and can save your life.
Ashe has few ways to escape. Dash in with Sweeping Blade through a minion and trade hard, since she can only slow you.
Do not walk up in a straight line in her Volley range. Stay behind minions so they absorb the arrows.
Hit minions with Steel Tempest to build the whirlwind, then use it to knock Ashe up from range when she steps forward.
Stay with your team when Ashe's Enchanted Crystal Arrow is ready, since a long-range hit stuns you for a long time.
Hold Wind Wall for Piltover Peacemaker and Ace in the Hole. It destroys projectiles that hit it.
Do not walk over bushes or open ground where Caitlyn may have placed Yordle Snap Trap. Dash with Sweeping Blade at a minion instead.
Build up Steel Tempest stacks on minions. Her long range means you must close the gap to threaten her with the whirlwind.
Dodge her net sideways, or dash with Sweeping Blade. It slows you and sets up a Headshot.
Cast Wind Wall when Ezreal shoots at you; it blocks Mystic Shot, Essence Flux and Trueshot Barrage.
Ezreal is fragile, so take the fight to him. Dash in with Sweeping Blade through a minion once his Arcane Shift is used.
Walk around while Ezreal is out of range to build your shield from Way of the Wanderer, then it absorbs his poke.
Stay behind minions so Ezreal's Mystic Shot stops on them, and step sideways to dodge his shots.
Cast Wind Wall across the lane when Jhin fires Deadly Flourish; it blocks enemy projectiles, so his long shot never lands.
Hold Wind Wall for Jhin's Dancing Grenade and his final shot of Curtain Call too, since both are blockable projectiles.
Walk in with Sweeping Blade right after Jhin fires his fourth shot; he must reload and cannot attack for a moment.
Step around Lotus Traps you suspect Jhin placed; they slow you and then explode. Dash through minions rather than into unseen ground.
Do not stay close to Jhin's allies' damage; once he has hit you, Deadly Flourish can leave you rooted, so keep Wind Wall ready.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Jinx fires Zap! or her Super Mega Death Rocket!; it blocks both before they land.
Dash onto Jinx with Sweeping Blade when she is poking with rockets; her minigun needs time to ramp up, so close in fast.
Walk around the side of Flame Chompers! instead of through them; one that goes off roots you in place.
Stay out of a straight line with Jinx so Zap! misses; being hit leaves you slowed and easy to kill.
Engage right after Jinx wastes Flame Chompers!; with it on cooldown she has little to stop you reaching her.
Hit minions with Steel Tempest to build your stacks, then throw the whirlwind through the enemy and knock them up.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Kai'Sa uses Void Seeker or her Icathian Rain; it destroys projectiles.
Do not dash in blindly with Sweeping Blade. Kai'Sa can hit you with Void Seeker, and a slow or stun while dashing knocks you down.
Look for her when she is alone. Kai'Sa is weaker without her team to stack Plasma, so go in on her then.
Keep your Last Breath for when your teammate knocks Kai'Sa up, then dive her.
Use Wind Wall to block Double Up and Make It Rain, especially when Miss Fortune is lining up a trade.
Dash onto her with Sweeping Blade through a minion, then use Steel Tempest. She is easy to kill once you reach her.
Hit her to cancel her Strut speed boost. Once it is gone she cannot easily run from you.
Hit minions with Steel Tempest to build stacks, then send the whirlwind at her. It knocks her up and can set up Last Breath.
Do not stand still in Make It Rain. Walk out of it quickly, since it slows you and hurts.
Leave the fight or use Wind Wall when Bullet Time starts. She cannot move while she channels it.
Wait until Sivir's Spell Shield is used before you commit with Steel Tempest or Sweeping Blade. Blocked abilities heal her.
Put up Wind Wall when Sivir throws Boomerang Blade at you. It stops the blade, and she loses a lot of mana.
Step sideways out of Boomerang Blade. If it hits you going out, stay out of its path as it comes back.
Do not chase Sivir after she attacks you. Her Fleet of Foot speed burst makes her hard to catch.
Look for a knock up from your support to use Last Breath. Sivir's Spell Shield will not stop it.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Smolder sneezes with Achooo!; it destroys the glob before it can slow you.
Hold Wind Wall for Super Scorcher Breath too; the fireball is a projectile the wall can block.
Smolder is weak early, so trade hard while his Dragon Practice stacks are low. Fighting later lets him grow into a big threat.
Dash onto Smolder with Sweeping Blade, then use Steel Tempest mid-dash to hit in a circle around you.
Hit Smolder with the Steel Tempest whirlwind to knock him up so you can follow with Last Breath at level 6.
Do not stand in a straight line from Smolder; sidestep Steel Tempest-style, narrow shots by moving sideways, not backward.
Put Wind Wall in front of you when Yunara throws her bead. It blocks projectiles, so you take no damage or slow from it.
Use Wind Wall against her basic attacks in a fight. They are projectiles, so the wall stops them.
Dash onto her with Sweeping Blade right after she has thrown her bead, then trade.
Stay out of a straight line with her bead, because it slows heavily on hit. Being slowed lets her attack freely.
Her Transcend One's Self lasts a short time. Back off and keep Wind Wall ready for the laser, then fight when it ends.
